title: When the Uniform Breaks
premise: In the winter of 1899, apprentice clockmaker Lena Underhill is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock and finds a sealed letter hidden in its case, naming her late father among conspirators who falsified astronomical records to protect a shipping magnate's fortunes. As she traces the letter's provenance, she must decide whether to expose a truth that will ruin the family of the man she loves, Inspector Elias Vane, whose duty-bound investigation is closing in on her. Racing the turn of the century, Lena secretly publishes the evidence through an underground press before the victors' historians can bury it. In the end she loses Elias to his badge but wins the record itself: the truth stands in print as the new century dawns, and she winds the master clock one last time on her own terms.
about_author: Jonah Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing municipal records in port cities, where he developed a fascination with the small clerical lies that history runs on. He writes historical fiction about ordinary tradespeople caught in machinery far larger than themselves.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Lena Underhill arrives at the observatory to repair the failing master clock, navigating the condescension of the astronomers who see only an apprentice. Inside the clock case she discovers a sealed letter dated 1884, bearing her father's name. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking a lifetime of practiced invisibility, now cracked by dread.

chapters.title: What the Letter Names
chapters.summary: Lena deciphers the letter at night: it implicates her father and three others in altering tidal and stellar records to conceal a shipwreck caused by the Halloran Shipping Company. She recognizes Inspector Elias Vane's family crest among the beneficiaries. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: the sick vertigo of learning that her father's silence was complicity, not protection.

chapters.title: An Inspector Calls at Dusk
chapters.summary: Elias Vane visits Lena's workshop, ostensibly about the observatory break-in reported by the astronomers; their old affection resurfaces beneath careful formality. She realizes he is investigating the same conspiracy from the other side. POV: alternating Lena and Elias. Emotional beat: tenderness strained by the knowledge that duty will eventually force them to choose.

chapters.title: The Historian's Ledger
chapters.summary: Lena seeks out Archibald Fenn, a retired observatory clerk living in disgrace, who confirms the records were falsified and that the victors are already commissioning a sanitized official history for the century's end. POV: Lena with Fenn's testimony. Emotional beat: grief hardening into resolve as she understands the race is against memory itself.

chapters.title: Silences That Keep People Safe
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: fifteen years earlier, young Lena learns from her father which questions never to ask after a client disappears. Present-day Lena recognizes she has inherited his survival strategy and rejects it. POV: Lena, dual timeline. Emotional beat: mourning the father she defended and breaking the inheritance of fear.

chapters.title: A Warrant in Winter
chapters.summary: Elias obtains a warrant to search the observatory archives; his superior quietly redirects him toward scapegoats, revealing how deep the corruption runs inside the constabulary. Elias begins keeping his own private file. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: the first hairline fracture in his faith in the law he serves.

chapters.title: The Underground Press
chapters.summary: Lena brings the evidence to Marguerite Osei, printer of an illegal broadsheet, who agrees to set the story but warns that publication means arrest warrants for them both. They begin typesetting by lamplight. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose; invisibility traded for solidarity.

chapters.title: Where Duty Points
chapters.summary: Elias discovers Lena's connection to the underground press and confronts her; she shows him the letter and his own family's name within it. Torn, he delays the raid on the print shop by falsifying his report, committing his first crime for justice. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: love and duty tearing in opposite directions, and duty losing.

chapters.title: The Last Night of the Century
chapters.summary: New Year's Eve, 1899: as the city celebrates, soldiers and inspectors close in on the print shop. Lena and Marguerite finish the final run as Elias holds the door, buying minutes with his career and nearly his life. The broadsheets flood the streets before midnight. POV: all three interwoven. Emotional beat: breathless climax, sacrifice, and triumph measured in ink.

chapters.title: Winding the Master Clock
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the scandal has broken the Halloran empire and disgraced the constabulary's command; Elias, dismissed, chooses exile over reinstatement, and he and Lena part without bitterness. Lena returns to the observatory, repairs the master clock fully, and sets it running into the new century. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—love lost, truth kept, time finally honest.
